Subject: Acme RAG eval  post-call recap, recommended models & reranker plan

Hi Jordan / Taylor,

Thanks again for the time today  great conversation and helpful context on the internal search use cases and SLAs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a lightweight eval/Sandbox run: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary use case: RAG-powered docs Q&A and internal knowledge search for product + support teams.
- Key constraints: high precision for grounded answers (auditability), latency SLO ~300ms for interactive flows, and support for multi-doc context (long docs and PDFs).
- Success metrics you care about: grounding precision@5, hallucination rate, and user-observed latency.

Redwood recommended starting configuration (for eval):
- Retriever: "open-rag-retriever-v2" using 1kB chunking (~800 tokens), with dense embeddings.
- Embedding model: "redwood-embed-large-v1" (good tradeoff for recall on mixed-format docs).
- Reranker: two-phase approach  bi-encoder for recall (top_k=150) + cross-encoder reranker for final top_n=5. We propose comparing:
  1) Bi-encoder only (fast, lower cost)
  2) Bi-encoder + small cross-encoder re-rank (better grounding)
  3) LLM-native rerank (for a small sample)
- Generation model candidates: Llama-2-70B-Chat (quantized) for highest-quality long-form answers, and a smaller cost-optimized baseline: Red-Chat-13B-Quant (recommended for interactive flows).
- Caching & latency: enable prefix KV caching and set batching window to 20ms for interactive endpoints.

Attachments and links: I attached an initial prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v2.csv) and a short benchmark overview (redwood-benchmarks-acme.pdf). Also sharing our benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=redwood-acme-benchmarks

Proposed next steps
1) We run a 3-day eval on a sandbox with your sample docs (we'll need 5-10 representative documents and a set of ~50 eval prompts).
2) Redwood SE (Dylan) will run the retrieval + reranker A/B and return grounding precision/hallucination metrics.
3) Quick sync next Tuesday to review results and pick a configuration for a 2-week pilot.

Can you send the sample doc pack and the 50-ish evaluation prompts? If you prefer, we can collect them via a secure upload link  happy to send.

Thanks 
Marissa Cole

Hi Jordan / Taylor  Dylan here (SE). Happy to take the 30-min sync  my availability Tuesday 1010am or Wednesday 24pm PT.

Quick answers to your questions: 
- Latency & cost tradeoffs (high level):
  * Bi-encoder only (top_k serving): lowest cost and predictable latency; good recall but lower final grounding precision because there's no expensive cross-attention rerank. Typical 95p latency for retrieval + generation pipeline: ~150 300ms depending on model size and caching.
  * Bi-encoder + cross-encoder rerank (top_k=150, rerank_top=5): higher cost (cross-encoder is O(N) with cross-attention) and added latency for rerank step; we see ~1.5 2x cost increase on the retrieval portion and ~50 150ms extra latency depending on infra. However, grounding precision@5 typically improves substantially (we often observe +8 20 pts depending on data).
  * LLM-native rerank: most expensive and highest latency but can simplify orchestration for small-scale pilots.

- Grounding metrics we recommend for the eval: 
  * Grounding Precision@k (GP@k): fraction of model answers where at least one of the top-k retrieved passages was actually used to produce the final grounded answer (automated via answer-passage alignment heuristics + manual spot checks).
  * Reference-based F1 against human labels for fact-sensitive answers.
  * Hallucination Rate: fraction of answers containing assertions not supported by retrieved passages (human-labeled sample).
  * Latency p95 and token-level cost.

Proposed eval plan (short):
- Step 0: Confirm sample docs + prompts (Jordan sends).
- Step 1: Index sample docs, run embedding + retrieval baseline (bi-encoder).
- Step 2: Run reranker A/B (bi-encoder only vs bi-encoder+cross-encoder).
- Step 3: Generate metrics (GP@5, hallucination rate, p95 latency).
- Step 4: Share results & recommend pilot config.

I attached our short eval plan (acme_rag_eval_plan.md) and will load a quick notebook into the shared Drive after we get the doc set.

If it helps, for the reranker we usually start with these defaults: top_k=150, rerank_top=5, chunk_size=800 tokens. For the bi-encoder we use "redwood-embed-large-v1" and for cross-encoder we use "redwood-reranker-cross-small-v1".

Happy to walk through the plan  happy to meet Tuesday at 10am PT.

Thanks,

Jordan / Taylor  Dev here (Applied ML). Couple quick technical notes for the eval run: 

- For automated GP@k we use two signals: exact-span overlap (automated) + semantic alignment via an embedding-similarity threshold. We then surface a human-labeled 10 15% spot-check for edge cases.
- Suggested Eval parameters: embedding dim 1536, chunk overlap 128 tokens, top_k retrieval=150, rerank_top=5.
- To speed iteration we can run the first pass with a smaller sample (20 prompts) and then scale to the full 50 once configs are locked.

I'll provision the sandbox and a reproducible notebook for the run once I have the sample docs. Expect an initial results deck within 72 hours of data receipt.
